A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same JanusCoder research work, with 41 pages including Appendices A–I. Text extraction and rendering support a complete comparison; pages 2–41 are identical, and the first-page changes are fully readable.

before.justification: V2 reports original JanusCoder and JanusCoderV benchmark results in Tables 3–4, ablations in Table 5, and human evaluations in Table 15.

after.justification: V3 retains the original model evaluations, ablations, supplementary analyses, and human-evaluation outcomes reported in v2.

M1.justification: The four synthesis strategies, execution checks, reward filtering, and JanusCoder/JanusCoderV procedures remain identical in Section 3 and Appendices A, C, E, and I.

E1.justification: JanusCode-800K's composition and the evaluated tasks remain unchanged, including chart generation, chart-to-code, web generation/editing, artifacts, dynamic visualizations, scientific demonstrations, and general coding.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding main-text and appendix experiments, including GPT-4o and Qwen/InternVL variants, VisCoder in Figures 5–6, and the human-evaluation baselines in Table 15.

E3.justification: Benchmark construction, metrics, sample sizes, model configurations, and training settings are unchanged, including the 102-task DTVBench and three-epoch training described in Section 4 and Appendix E.

E4.justification: Both retain identical data/reward ablations, backbone and general-coding analyses, cross-model adjudication, human evaluation, and case studies (Section 6; Appendices G–H; Figures 4–10).

E5.justification: Table 14 retains identical judge-score variance and Krippendorff's alpha reporting. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-test reporting is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings, and generated examples are unchanged, including appendix results. For example, Table 3 retains JanusCoder-14B's 9.7% incorrect-code rate and task score of 86 on PandasPlotBench.

T1.justification: The synthesis and reward definitions in Section 3, DTVBench scoring formula in Section 4.2, and TreeBLEU expression in Appendix F.4 are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about a unified visual-programmatic interface, the largest multimodal code corpus, and 7B–14B models approaching or exceeding commercial-model performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of cross-domain synergy, reward filtering, backbone generality, judge agreement, and visual-versus-structural fidelity remain unchanged in Section 6 and Appendices F–G. No new limitations or applicability qualifications appear.

D1.justification: V2 provides one GitHub link for code and checkpoints. V3 retains that code destination and adds separate direct Hugging Face links to the checkpoint collection and JanusCode-800K dataset on page 1. Implementation and training disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, and the bibliography are identical. Positioning against approaches specialized for isolated visual coding tasks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: First-page edits standardize 'multi-modal' to 'multimodal', replace the closing availability sentence with resource labels, and update the arXiv version/date. Other prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Page 1 reflows the abstract and adds an icon-labeled row for Code, Checkpoints, and JanusCode-800K. All numbered figures, tables, and page layouts on pages 2–41 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: V3 improves resource-location documentation by adding explicit checkpoint-collection and dataset links alongside the retained code link. This provides a limited usability benefit; scientific content and supporting evidence remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish live resource availability.
